results.title: Cheapest H100 and B200 Cloud: CoreWeave vs Nebius vs Lambda vs Crusoe · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

Among CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe, the cheapest on-demand H100 on November 3, 2026 was Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour, then Lambda at $3.99 (8x instance), Nebius at $4.50 and CoreWeave at $6.16 (an 8-GPU node at $49.24 an hour). Crusoe's page says its H100 rises to $4.50 on December 1, 2026. The cheapest on-demand B200 was Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x; $6.99 on one GPU), then Nebius at $8.50 and CoreWeave at $8.60; Crusoe's B200 is contact-sales. For interruptible work, CoreWeave's spot nodes work out to $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200, and Nebius preemptible starts from $0.79 (H100) and $0.99 (B200) at a dynamic rate. Smaller clouds go lower still: Hyperstack listed a B200 at $6.00 and an H100 at $2.50.

- Cheapest H100 on demand: Crusoe $3.90 (until Dec 1), Lambda $3.99 (8x), single H100 PCIe at Lambda $3.29
- Cheapest B200 on demand: Lambda $6.69 (8x) to $6.99 (1x)
- Most expensive on demand: CoreWeave, $6.16 per H100 and $8.60 per B200
- Cheapest if you can be interrupted: CoreWeave spot, $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200; Nebius preemptible is dynamic
- Below the big four: Hyperstack B200 $6.00, H100 $2.50; Vast.ai H100 SXM from $2.40

...

- B200 on demand, per GPU-hour: Lambda $6.69 (8x) to $6.99 (1x), Nebius $8.50, CoreWeave $8.60, Crusoe contact sales.
- CoreWeave charges 58% more than Crusoe and 54% more than Lambda for an on-demand H100, and 29% more than Lambda for a B200 (our arithmetic from the published prices).
- Crusoe's page lists new on-demand prices starting Dec 1, 2026: H100 $3.90 to $4.50, H200 $4.29 to $5.40, B300 $8.96 to $9.90.
- CoreWeave's public prices are for whole 8-GPU nodes; Lambda's price table lists separate single-GPU (1x) prices for the H100 and B200.

...

## Is there anything cheaper than the big four?

For the H100, yes, by a lot. For the B200, only some.

- Hyperstack listed on-demand H100 at $2.50 (PCIe), $2.60 (NVLink) and $3.20 (SXM), H200 SXM at $3.99, B200 at $6.00 and B300 at $7.40 per hour on Nov 3, 2026. That B200 price is the lowest data-center on-demand B200 we found on a public price list that day.
- GMI Cloud listed H100 from $2.60 and H200 from $3.20 per GPU-hour; its B200 "from $5.00" is marked contact sales.
- Runpod (Secure Cloud pods) listed H100 PCIe at $2.89, H100 SXM at $3.99, H200 at $5.29 and B200 at $7.99 per hour. The same page's product data also lists Community Cloud rates (B200 $5.98, H100 PCIe $1.99), but its docs say "Runpod is no longer accepting new hosts for Community Cloud. Existing Community Cloud resources remain available," so that capacity is limited to the hosts already there.
- Vast.ai, a marketplace, had H100 SXM from $2.40 and H100 PCIe from $2.54 per hour on demand in our 15:20 UTC read on Nov 3, 2026. Its cheapest on-demand B200 was $10.25, more than any big cloud, so the marketplace isn't the cheap route for Blackwell right now.

...

Every big-cloud price is the provider's published rate on its own pricing page, read on Nov 3, 2026, before sales tax, in US dollars. CoreWeave per-GPU figures are its 8-GPU node prices divided by eight (North America). "From" prices are floors, and spot and preemptible prices move. Vast and Runpod prices come from our own price feed (snapshot 15:20 UTC, Nov 3, 2026), which also powers the compare page. A listed price doesn't guarantee capacity. We earn referral fees from Vast and Runpod, not from CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, Hyperstack or GMI Cloud, and that doesn't change any number on this page.

highlights:
packet.ai Team August 26, 2026

Hyperstack H100 SXM on-demand costs $3.20/hr in August 2026. packet.ai B200 on-demand costs $4.25/hr - Blackwell-generation hardware for 33% more than Hyperstack's Hopper H100 rate. Hyperstack B200 costs $6.00/hr. The hyperstack pricing gap on Blackwell is where this comparison starts.

Key takeaways

- Hyperstack on-demand GPU pricing from hyperstack.cloud/gpu-pricing (August 2026): H100 SXM $3.20/hr, H200 SXM $3.99/hr, A100 PCIe $1.35/hr, B200 $6.00/hr, B300 $7.40/hr. No spot pricing. Reserved rates apply with commitment. B200 and B300 are self-serve; GB200 and Vera Rubin NVL72 are quote-only.
- packet.ai B200 on-demand: $4.25/hr. Hyperstack B200 on-demand: $6.00/hr. For Blackwell access without a quote process, packet.ai is 29% cheaper on the same generation hardware.
- packet.ai RTX 6000 Pro: $0.76/hr. Hyperstack RTX Pro 6000 SE: $1.85/hr. Same 96GB VRAM class, 59% price difference. For teams running 70B QLoRA inference on a single card, that gap compounds across long runs.
- Hyperstack has no spot or preemptible pricing tier. Every GPU hour is billed at on-demand or reserved rates. For interruptible training workloads where spot saves 50-70%, Hyperstack has no equivalent path.
- Hyperstack covers EU West, UK, and US East only. No APAC. For teams in India, Southeast Asia, or Australia-Pacific, Hyperstack introduces latency with no data residency benefit. packet.ai APAC capacity launches Q3 2026.
- Hyperstack VM hibernation is a genuine differentiator: pause a GPU VM and stop billing for compute while retaining disk state. No equivalent on most neocloud alternatives including packet.ai currently.

# GPU Rental Prices — Week of August 17 - August 23, 2026

Weekly snapshot of GPU rental pricing across 35 marketplaces, August 17 - August 23, 2026. Observable data only — no estimates, no predictions.

By Lucas Zelko• Ai Mining Co.

B300 SXM median hourly rates rose 2.0% week-over-week, from $7.50 to $7.65, the largest percentage move among any SKU tracked by Ai Mining Co. during the August 17–23 observation window. The advance was modest in absolute terms but stood out across an otherwise subdued pricing environment: H100 SXM and H200 SXM both held flat at $3.20 and $4.59 per GPU-hour respectively, while the remaining top movers registered gains of 1.1% or less. AIMC tracked 8,138 observations across 35 reporting marketplaces and 113 distinct GPU SKUs during the period, providing a broad cross-section of the spot rental market. Price dispersion within individual GPU families remained wide — L40S listings ranged from $0.63 to $2.48 per GPU-hour across 14 marketplaces — a pattern that warrants closer examination across the major families covered below.

The cross-GPU price movement observed during the week of August 17–23 reveals a pattern worth examining closely. AIMC's data shows that out of 8,138 observations across 35 marketplaces, upward price movement was concentrated at the two ends of the performance spectrum: the newest frontier hardware and older consumer-grade silicon moved in tandem, while mid-tier workhorses held flat. The B300 SXM led all movers at +2.0% ($7.50 to $7.65), the B200 SXM followed at +1.0% ($6.11 to $6.17), and simultaneously the RTX 3090 ticked up +0.7% ($0.44 to $0.45) and the RTX A4000 gained the same +0.7% ($0.27 to $0.28). Against this, the H100 SXM and H200 SXM both closed the week completely flat. That divergence — frontier and budget moving, mid-tier stationary — is a pattern the data surfaces but does not fully explain.

This report contains observable market data only. No estimates, no forecasts, no buy/sell recommendations.

All fifteen priced providers were unchanged from Issue 006, producing a zero-movement priced panel in the August 10 observation.

The two repricings recorded in Issue 006 also held again. Hyperstack remained at $3.20 after its move from $2.40, and RunPod Secure Cloud remained at $2.99 after its move from $3.29. On the evidence to date, both changes look persistent rather than like one-cycle anomalies.

## Track 2 under A1-R1.

Issue 007 is a priced-only observation under the two-track cadence adopted August 10 and approved August 11, 2026. The twelve providers excluded at Issue 006 were not recaptured in this Track 2 cycle. Their dispositions carry from the full twenty-seven-provider sweep sealed July 21, and their next full re-verification is due on or about August 21.

The scheduled slots of July 27 and August 3 were not observed. Under A1-R1 the skipped slots force no full sweep and are disclosed here. Movement in Issue 007 is stated against Issue 006.

The SVCI observes public, fixed, on-demand rates for the H100 SXM 80GB-class anchor across a twenty-seven-provider universe in three tiers, from logged-out surfaces only. Quote-gated, from-floor, spot, committed and account-gated figures never enter a median. Full-machine prices divide to per-GPU in recorded arithmetic. Providers without a comparable public rate are excluded and disclosed, not estimated. Under A1-R1, priced-provider observations are captured fresh on weekly or biweekly issue cycles, while the full twenty-seven-provider panel is re-verified on a monthly clock.

results.title: Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1 | Beyond the News
highlights:
# Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1

Fireworks' current pricing table shows September 1 increases across H100, H200, B200, B300 and GB300 on-demand deployments, with B200 rising from $10 to $13 per GPU-hour. Dedicated training jobs that use the same GPU-hour rates inherit the new economics.

Reviewed and published by Lars Jansen Updated 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 4 min read Copy link

 First published 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 

## Key details

1. The new Fireworks on-demand GPU rates begin September 1, 2026.
2. H100 80GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
3. H200 141GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
4. B200 180GB: $10 → $13 per GPU-hour.
5. B300 288GB: $12 → $15 per GPU-hour.
6. GB300 288GB: $18 → $20 per GPU-hour.
7. On-demand deployments are billed per GPU second with no extra startup charges.
8. Region-restricted deployments are priced at a 1.5× premium.
9. Dedicated Training API jobs use the same on-demand GPU-hour pricing.

...

## What changed

Fireworks' current pricing page publishes a two-column transition for its on-demand GPU deployments: prices through August 31 and new rates from September 1, 2026. H100 80GB and H200 141GB increase from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour; B200 180GB rises from $10 to $13; B300 288GB from $12 to $15; and GB300 288GB from $18 to $20. Fireworks bills on-demand deployments per GPU second with no startup charge, and its Dedicated Training API uses the same GPU-hour pricing, so the change affects both dedicated serving and GPU-hour training jobs. Region-restricted deployments continue to carry a 1.5× premium.

...

Dedicated GPU economics can dominate the unit cost of high-volume inference, fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning workloads. These increases range from roughly 11% to 30%, large enough to change break-even points between accelerator generations, serverless APIs and competing GPU clouds. The biggest increase is on B200, where a workload consuming 1,000 GPU-hours per month moves from $10,000 to $13,000 before regional premiums or other services. Teams should therefore benchmark completed-task throughput rather than choosing hardware on hourly price or peak specifications alone.

## The September increase varies materially by accelerator

H100 and H200 move from $7 to $8 per hour, about a 14.3% increase. B200 rises 30% from $10 to $13, B300 rises 25% from $12 to $15 and GB300 rises about 11.1% from $18 to $20. The uneven changes can alter the relative cost ranking of GPUs even when performance remains unchanged.

...

Fireworks states that Dedicated Training API jobs are priced per GPU hour using the On-Demand Pricing section. Teams running reinforcement fine-tuning or dedicated training should therefore update both serving and training forecasts, not only inference deployment budgets.

...

On-demand deployments are billed by the second and do not charge extra startup time, which remains useful for bursty workloads. But sustained fleets still absorb the full hourly increase, and a region-restricted deployment costs 1.5 times the listed rate.

...

A more expensive accelerator can still win if it materially improves throughput, latency or batch efficiency. Builders should compare cost per successful request, training run or completed agent task under the exact model, quantization, context and concurrency they use.
